method: One L40, resident identical FP32 inputs, fresh construction in separate sequential processes. Three warmups and five synchronized measured calls per backend/case, except native Bicycle and Playroom: one warmup and three measured calls. That fixed long-case schedule was selected after a 174-second native Bicycle warmup, before collecting its timed samples; the preliminary warmup record is retained. Allocation included; preceding result destroyed before each call; JIT/upload/download/validation excluded. Warp allocator retains 32 GiB. Torch intra/inter-op and OMP/MKL/OpenBLAS thread counts are one. Both visible CPU quotas are four cores. All 86 primary measured calls have zero throttled periods; only the benchmark CUDA process was observed at each GPU snapshot. GPU events are elapsed spans, including idle gaps, not kernel sums.
qualification: WarPower and Paragram return bounded Voronoi neighbor CSR in original input order, using box padding 1.00001 and 1.0 respectively. Native RadFoam returns unbounded neighbor CSR plus tetrahedra and a permutation, in internally sorted order. Native-to-Warp ratios compare these construction calls, not identical outputs, incremental updates, tetrahedron construction alone, or fitting speed.
preflight: A separate 10-call Bonsai native preflight recorded CPU throttling in one call; all ten calls and its runner are retained. An initial Garden native window overlapped another agent's Warp tests and recorded CPU throttling; it is excluded. Bicycle's following run was interrupted during warmup when competing GPU activity was observed. Both records are retained. Primary results use the fixed windows described above after contention ends. Profiling is separate from primary timing.
